title: Best Looking Slabs (2026)
verdict: The best looking slabs are a matter of taste, and AGS makes our list first for a clear PMMA holder that puts the card ahead of the label.

Looks are personal. TAG's holder has no paper label at all, with the card ID inscribed in clear acrylic. SGC's black insert frames vintage better than anything else. Beckett prints subgrades on a heavy slab. PSA's plain holder is the one buyers know best.

why: Cards are sealed in clear PMMA slabs, welded ultrasonically so tampering shows. The label carries the grade and cert number. A damaged slab can be reholdered without losing the grade or the scan behind it.

AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

You see why the card got its grade. AGS issues eight subgrades, four for the front and four for the back, plus a defect list and a 3D heightmap. Most graders hand back one number. A buyer who can open the report has less to argue about.

faq.q: Which grading company has the best looking slabs?
faq.a: It is subjective. Collectors often name TAG for its clear, label-free holder and SGC for its black insert. AGS uses a clear PMMA slab with an ultrasonic seal. Pick the one you like on a shelf.

faq.q: How do I verify an AGS slab?
faq.a: Enter the cert number from the label on agscard.com. The record shows the grade and the scan report for that card.

faq.q: Can I cross a card over from another grader's slab?
faq.a: CGC and Ace Grading list crossover services. AGS's FAQ does not list one, so ask AGS before sending a card in another company's holder.

faq.q: What are AGS slabs made of?
faq.a: PMMA plastic, sealed with tamper-evident ultrasonic welds. All graded cards are slabbed.

faq.q: Can a damaged slab be replaced?
faq.a: Yes. AGS offers a reholder service for cracked or scratched slabs. The grade and digital record stay with the card.
